system.biography:
Jaz Kaur knows the city by the weight of a bag on her shoulders: the climb towards Highbury, the headwind off the Lea, the dangerous pause before a driver opens a door. She used to deliver the things other people forgot. Now Pat asks her to collect things their owners have not forgotten at all.

Her family thinks the workshop job has finally steadied her. It has, in a way. The Chainring pays in cash, fixes her bike without asking, and does not penalise her for taking ten minutes to help someone at the roadside. She is determined to make enough for a legitimate garage before the favours begin to own her.

Contacts: Spanner Rob gives her parts and honest advice. Kez supplies delivery gossip. Mo Rahman sometimes lets her leave a bag behind his counter. Friction: Stretch says she owes him for a scrambler she insists was already wrecked. DS Vale remembers her face from a witness statement.

Crew bond: Danny talked her out of an arrest after a late-night collision. Femi once waited with her through an unpaid shift. Sal has become the person she calls when a customer will not give a bicycle back.

system.biography:
Danny Doyle acquired “Tealeaf” long before he could afford anything worth stealing. He can mend a stuck shop shutter, find a missing set of keys, and tell a convincing story about why he was near either of them. He has never decided whether this is talent or simply a failure to imagine a different trade.

Pat gave him work after a short sentence and a very long silence from his old employer. Danny is grateful enough to be dangerous: he would rather lie to his friends than admit a job has gone beyond him. His current debt is a few hundred pounds, a handful of favours and one account he does not discuss.

Contacts: Auntie Pat protects him but keeps an exact ledger. Mo offers odd jobs. Kez laughs at his scams and remembers every detail. Enemy: Stretch is buying up small debts around the Lea and has Danny’s name on a list.

Crew bond: He made the phone call that got Jaz out of trouble, which he mentions less often than she expects. Femi can tell when he is frightened. He trusts Sal to ask the question he is avoiding.

system.biography:
Femi Adebayo can calm a room before anyone notices he has entered it. He has spent years listening to frightened people, recognising when a story is about to turn ugly, and doing the small practical thing that keeps a bad evening from becoming a disaster. The pay for those skills has never kept pace with the rent.

He told himself the first bike was only a way to catch up. The second had a buyer before he touched it. He still draws lines: no work that endangers children, no abandoning an injured person, and no guns in the flat. Keeping those lines may cost more than crossing them.

Contacts: Mo Rahman gives him quiet warnings about the neighbourhood. A paramedic friend will answer a question, but cannot make evidence disappear. DS Harriet Vale knows Femi has helped at an incident; she would prefer him on her side of a statement. Rival: the Lea Boys dislike anyone who stops a frightened debtor from paying.

Crew bond: He treats Jaz’s crashes without a lecture, worries about Danny’s silences, and knows Sal’s bluster hides a practical kindness. He wants this crew to become people who can stop doing this.

identity.vice: Cannot let an insult to a friend go
identity.bond: Pat gave them work after the venue closed.

system.biography:
Big Sal Moretti used to finish a shift with a pocketful of crumpled notes and somebody else’s blood on their cuff. Closing the venue did not remove their talent for moving trouble away from a door. Pat needed a driver who could carry a washing machine alone. Sal needed regular money and a place where showing up counted.

They dislike cruelty, grandstanding and being mistaken for someone who has not thought things through. When Sal says “leave it”, the crew would be wise to listen. They have a little money put aside for a café and an old address book that makes the idea look less fanciful than it sounds.

Contacts: Spanner keeps the van alive. Pat knows where the spare key is. A former door supervisor can find a room when Sal needs one. Enemy: Stretch hired Sal for a collection once and was furious when the money went back to the frightened tenant.

Crew bond: Sal sees Jaz as the driver they might have been, Danny as a problem worth solving, and Femi as the only person likely to get them all through the night without becoming someone else.

system.biography:
She knows every bicycle in the borough, including the ones she has not seen yet. Tea before business. Cash after inspection.

Pat wants a crew that earns quietly. She can source tools, buy stolen bicycles and set orders through the Blower. She expects loyalty, not cruelty.

Workshop mechanic, dry wit, permanent mug of tea.

Spanner repairs the crew’s kit and notices mismatched stories as readily as mismatched wheels. He knows Jaz is better than the work she is doing.

A sharp-eyed runner whose phone is always vibrating.

Kez trades information: where the bikes are, which road is closed, who is suddenly spending money. Treat them as a person with ambitions, not an infallible quest marker.

Chicken Palace’s owner. Friendly, observant, impossible to rush.

Mo lets the crew use the flat upstairs. He needs the downstairs business kept out of whatever is happening above it. He will help Femi, but will not lie about an injury.

The Lea Boys’ lanky organiser. Never raises his voice when someone else is watching.

Stretch buys debts, recruits frightened people and calls it opportunity. He wants Pat’s routes and believes Danny is the cheapest way in.

system.description: Easy to hide. Drawing it changes what kind of night this is.
A thick work coat. Better than a T-shirt when trouble starts.

system.biography:
A local runner in Stretch’s orbit.

Not a disposable enemy: give them a name, a reason to be here and a way out of the encounter. Grit and numbers, rather than military discipline.

DS Harriet Vale, sharp suit under a tired coat. Patient, methodical, difficult to charm twice.

Vale follows patterns: the same bicycles, the same van, the same frightened witnesses. She can become an antagonist or an uneasy ally. She offers choices and records the consequences.
